name: Session cookie without SameSite protection
description:
The response sets a cookie that carries a session identifier or bearer token (by its name, or because its value is a signed JWT) without an effective SameSite restriction: the attribute is missing, has a value browsers do not recognise, or is SameSite=None without Secure.

A cookie without SameSite is attached to requests that other sites cause the browser to make. Firefox and Safari send it on every cross-site request; Chrome treats it as Lax but still sends it on a cross-site top-level POST within two minutes of the cookie being set. That is the precondition for cross-site request forgery, and for cross-site leaks that read the authenticated state of a page. SameSite=None without Secure is ignored by current browsers, so the session cookie is not stored at all there, while older browsers store it and send it cross-site.

This row is burpsy's own: Burp's catalogue has no SameSite row. It is classified under CWE-1275.
remediation: Set SameSite=Lax (or Strict where cross-site navigation into an authenticated page is not needed) on session cookies. Where a cookie genuinely has to be sent in a cross-site context, set SameSite=None; Secure explicitly and protect state-changing requests with anti-CSRF tokens. Do not rely on a browser's default.
